title: Keeping yourself effective in a leading role
moduleTitle: Shared: Growing and managing a team
audience: Leads carrying a heavy load, or anyone wanting to stay effective across many years in the role.
learningOutcomes: Distinguish burnout from burn-down and name a warning sign for each.
Write a personal development plan that lists weaknesses, goals and support.
Plan personal time and an outside source of support as part of the role.

instruction.heading: Burnout and burn-down
instruction.body: Burnout comes from long periods of overload, frustration and time pressure. It is usually easy to notice because the leader feels exhausted and wants to stop. Burn-down is quieter. The leader still cares about the work but has lost the energy and drive that once came with it. Because burn-down shows less, it can go unnoticed for longer. Both affect the crew, because a lead who has lost energy stops giving clear direction and stops noticing problems.

instruction.heading: Personal development
instruction.body: Begin with an honest inventory of shortcomings, including recent ones that caused trouble. Group related weaknesses so they feel manageable, for example communication under pressure. Note the strengths you can build on. Turn each weakness into specific goals with dates. Find a mentor who will be candid with you and keep you to your deadlines. Use training the business provides, and ask for support for training that fits the plan.

instruction.heading: Time away and shared load
instruction.body: A lead who never switches off eventually makes poor decisions. Schedule time away from work that you can rely on, and protect it. Share the load by building up one or two capable crew members who can cover routine decisions. Looking for a peer group of other leads to talk with about the realities of the role can help you avoid isolation. Asking for help is part of doing the job well, not a sign of failure.

procedure: List the signs you have noticed in yourself that could point to burnout or burn-down.
Write a list of weaknesses, grouped into categories, and a list of strengths.
Turn two weaknesses into specific goals with dates and milestones.
Identify a mentor and agree a check-in schedule.
Schedule regular time away from work and note who covers your duties.
Review the plan at a set date and adjust it.

workedExamples.situation: A crew lead has covered every shift for four months and now feels little interest in new ideas for the crew.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What signs suggest burn-down, and what two actions should the lead take first?
workedExamples.reasoning: Loss of interest with continued commitment points to burn-down. The first actions are to share two routine decisions with a capable crew member and to book time away that the lead can rely on. A mentor check-in is set for two weeks later to review progress.

equipmentAndPpe: Notebook or planner. No specialist equipment.

commonErrors.error: Treating exhaustion as a personal failing rather than a workload problem.
commonErrors.prevention: Look at the workload and the support available before blaming yourself.

commonErrors.error: Never taking time away from the role.
commonErrors.prevention: Book time away in advance and name a cover person.

commonErrors.error: Writing a development plan with no dates or measures.
commonErrors.prevention: Give each goal a date and a measure.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Support for mental health and any workers' compensation claim depends on the business and the law.
A lead who is too tired to work safely must hand over the duties and tell the supervisor.

qualityStandard: The personal development plan has at least two goals with dates and measures.
The learner has identified a mentor and a planned time away from the role.
documentationEvidence: Personal development plan with goals, dates and mentor.
Time-away plan naming the cover person.
summary: Burnout shows as exhaustion; burn-down shows as lost drive that can go unnoticed.
Convert shortcomings into dated goals, and identify a mentor who will hold you to them.
Protect time away and share routine decisions so the role is sustainable.

knowledgeChecks.question: What distinguishes burn-down from burnout?
options: Burn-down is usually caused by a single client complaint and the crew does not know about it
Burn-down means the leader has been dismissed from the business for the whole year and their pay
Burn-down is a loss of drive that is harder to spot, with the person still caring about the work
Burn-down only affects new leaders and only in the first year of work in the job each time

knowledgeChecks.question: What makes a personal development goal useful?
options: It is written in general terms only
It is kept private, so no one checks
It depends on a single meeting today
It is specific, dated and has a measure

knowledgeChecks.question: What is a sound way for a lead to protect their capacity over time?
options: Share routine decisions with a capable crew member and plan regular time away
Work every shift to show commitment and never take a day off in the year
Stop asking for help from the crew and the other leads at all today
Avoid any contact with other leads and keep the crew away from them
